bibl.title: The Polyvalent Nature of the Alexandrian Elite Hypogea: A Case Study in the Greco-Egyptian Cultural Interaction in the Hellenistic and Roman Periods.
bibl.seg: Kyriakos Savvopoulos, The Polyvalent Nature of the Alexandrian Elite Hypogea: A Case Study in the Greco-Egyptian Cultural Interaction in the Hellenistic and Roman Periods.
Rogério Sousa, Maria do Céu Fialho, Mona Haggag & Nuno Simões Rodrigues (edd.), Alexandrea ad Aegyptum. The Legacy of Multiculturalism in Antiquity (Porto, 2013) pp. 101-121, figg.
bibl.note: The origins of the Alexandrian hypogea reconsidered in the light of new evidence. - The Mustapha Kamel Tomb I: a funerary mansion dedicated to heyday of hellenism in Aegypto. - The Anfushi necropolis: an elite Egyptian-Alexandrian option for a blessed afterlife. - Living as Alexandrian, dying as an Egyptian, facing the Roman: reflections of advanced multiculturalism in the elite hypogea of Roman Alexandria. - Hellenization, Egyptianization and Romanization towards Alexandrianization.
